top_stories.title: Microsoft’s September Identity Batch Proves the Authentication Gap Is Not an Open-Source Problem
top_stories.summary: Microsoft disclosed nine out-of-cycle vulnerabilities on September 3, 2026, including two rated CVSS 10.0: CVE-2026-83711, an authorization bypass in Azure AD B2C, and CVE-2026-70352. The disclosures directly affect Microsoft's identity platform and highlight critical authentication and authorization vulnerabilities in enterprise IAM infrastructure.

top_stories.title: Identity-Based AI Attack Threatens Security of Enterprise Data
top_stories.summary: A new attack technique called "workflow identity hijacking" has been identified that can bypass standard security controls by exploiting unauthenticated entry points to compromise enterprise data. The attack targets identity-based weaknesses in AI workflows, allowing attackers to hijack organizational data through basic requests that circumvent authentication mechanisms.

top_stories.title: MFA's Weakest Link: Account Recovery Is the New Attack Path
top_stories.summary: Attackers are increasingly targeting account recovery processes as a bypass for MFA, exploiting weaknesses in password reset and authentication method recovery workflows. Specops outlines why stronger identity verification at the service desk is necessary to prevent social engineering attacks from converting account recovery into account takeover.

top_stories.title: Hackers deploy Linux rootkit on F5 BIG-IP APM devices, hiding web shell in memory
top_stories.summary: Hackers have deployed a Linux rootkit on F5 BIG-IP APM devices that hides a web shell in memory rather than writing it to disk, as reported by Sophos. F5 BIG-IP APM is an access policy management platform used by enterprises, financial institutions, and government agencies to secure access to applications, APIs, and data.

top_stories.title: FreeIPA Flaw Chain Lets Anonymous Clients Create Reusable Administrator Credentials
top_stories.summary: A vulnerability chain in FreeIPA allows anonymous, unauthenticated clients to create arbitrary Kerberos identities and gain membership in the administrators group. The attack combines a FreeIPA flaw with a second vulnerability in the 389 Directory Server (LDAP backend), as disclosed by Red Hat.

news.title: EU Cyber Resilience Act to Enforce New Reporting Requirements
news.summary: The EU Cyber Resilience Act introduces mandatory 24-hour reporting requirements for serious product security incidents, taking effect immediately. Businesses operating in the EU must notify government authorities within 24 hours of discovering qualifying security incidents, creating new compliance obligations for technology vendors including IAM product providers.

news.title: Cybercriminals are building phishing pages that exist only inside victims’ browsers
news.summary: Researchers at Barracuda identified a phishing campaign that exploits Microsoft OAuth and Teams infrastructure, using browser-generated blob URLs to assemble fake login pages locally in memory rather than serving them from a web server. This technique makes the malicious content harder to detect by traditional security tools since no phishing page exists on an external server.

news.title: Cisco confirms CVE-2026-20079 Secure FMC flaw exploited in attacks
news.summary: Cisco has confirmed that CVE-2026-20079, a maximum-severity authentication bypass vulnerability in its Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) software, is being actively exploited. The flaw allows attackers to bypass authentication controls in the FMC platform, which manages firewall policies and network security configurations.

news.title: Akeyless adds real-time enforcement for AI agents in production
news.summary: Akeyless has announced the general availability of Akeyless Agentic Runtime Authority, a real-time identity control layer for AI agent actions. The product enforces intent-based access control to restrict what AI agents can do once they have access, building on top of Akeyless SecretlessAI which brokers credential access to enterprise systems.

news.title: Orchid Security targets AI agent risk with drift detection and kill switches
news.summary: Orchid Security has launched identity drift detection and application-level kill switches designed to manage AI agent risk within enterprise environments. The controls address identity debt issues such as hard-coded credentials, orphaned accounts, unmanaged authentication paths, and excessive permissions that AI agents can exploit without breaking existing security controls.

news.title: Infostealer Logs Expose Replayable AI Tokens That Can Bypass MFA
news.summary: Cybercriminals are using infostealer malware logs (such as Lumma Stealer and Vidar) to harvest replayable AI session tokens and API keys from compromised systems, enabling account takeover of AI platforms like Google and Anthropic. These stolen tokens can bypass MFA controls by replaying valid session credentials, circumventing authentication protections entirely.

news.title: F5 BIG-IP APM Malware Injects a PHP Web Shell Into Memory, Evading Disk Scans
news.summary: Sophos published an analysis revealing that malware targeting F5 BIG-IP Access Policy Manager (APM) appliances injects a PHP web shell into memory rather than onto disk, bypassing file-based security scans. The malware hooks into Apache's PHP script loading process on the APM appliance, meaning the on-disk files appear clean while the in-memory versions are compromised.

news.title: firezone headless-client-1.5.12
news.summary: Firezone released version 1.5.12 of its headless client for its zero-trust access platform built on WireGuard. This is a minor versioned release of the open-source enterprise zero-trust networking product.

news.title: Autonomous AI Agents Compromise Thousands of Credentials in Under Six Hours
news.summary: A financially motivated threat actor used an autonomous multi-agent AI framework to harvest thousands of credentials in under six hours, according to Google Threat Intelligence Group. The attack demonstrates AI being weaponized for large-scale credential compromise, directly impacting authentication and identity security.

news.title: eMazzanti Technologies' Messaging Architects Partners with miniOrange to Deliver Unified Identity and Access Management for Legacy and Hybrid IT Environments
news.summary: eMazzanti Technologies' Messaging Architects division has partnered with miniOrange to deliver IAM solutions including SSO, MFA, PAM, and Zero Trust security. The partnership targets organizations running on-premises systems, GroupWise, and hybrid SaaS environments.

news.title: Fake IT Calls Target Executives in Microsoft 365 Data Theft and Extortion Attacks
news.summary: A threat cluster is conducting data theft and extortion attacks targeting Microsoft 365 by combining IT help desk vishing calls, adversary-in-the-middle token theft, and residential-proxy sign-ins. The campaign specifically targets executive-level staff such as directors and vice presidents, exploiting SaaS authentication mechanisms to steal session tokens and bypass MFA controls.

news.title: The End of the Authentication Gap: Microsoft’s SSPR Enforcement
news.summary: Microsoft Entra ID will terminate the use of unregistered directory contact data for self-service password reset (SSPR) as of September 7, 2026. Mobile numbers, business phones, and secondary emails not explicitly registered as authentication methods will no longer be usable for SSPR, requiring organizations to ensure users have properly registered authentication methods.

news.title: Okta Jumps 20% as AI-Driven Security Fears Fuel a Beat-and-Raise Quarter
news.summary: Okta shares surged up to 29% after the company beat fiscal Q2 estimates, with adjusted EPS of $1.05 versus $0.97 expected and revenue rising 11% to $805 million. The company also issued a raise in forward guidance, with AI-driven security concerns cited as a demand driver for Okta's identity security products.

news.title: Old, Unpatched Flaws Give Attackers Access to Philippines Nuclear Agency
news.summary: Threat actors exploited unpatched vulnerabilities in ownCloud to breach the Philippines Nuclear Agency, stealing reactor databases, personnel records, and credential stores. The attack leveraged commodity flaws to gain initial access, with credential stores among the compromised data.

news.title: Attackers Pounce on Critical Artifactory Bug Following Disclosure
news.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-82329) has been disclosed in JFrog Artifactory, allowing attackers to gain admin-level access on affected systems. Active exploitation has been observed following public disclosure of the flaw.

news.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
news.summary: A dark web service is selling digital scans of over 153 million drivers licenses from the US and Canada, apparently sourced from a Louisiana-based identity verification company. The FBI's New Orleans field office has opened an official inquiry into the breach, which directly implicates an identity verification provider's data handling practices.

news.title: Anthropic Users Hit by Infostealer Attacks, Session Thefts
news.summary: A threat actor deployed infostealer malware to steal session tokens and gain unauthorized access to Claude (Anthropic) user accounts. The attack targeted session credentials rather than passwords, bypassing standard authentication controls.

news.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
news.summary: Canadian hacker Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy charges related to breaching over 165 organizations using Snowflake cloud storage, including stealing call and text records of over 100 million AT&T customers. The attacks targeted organizations through compromised credentials accessing Snowflake accounts, which is relevant to IAM professionals as a case study in cloud account security and authentication controls.

news.title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
news.summary: CISA released a postmortem report on a data breach in which a contractor publicly exposed dozens of internal CISA credentials, including AWS GovCloud keys, in a GitHub repository for nearly six months. The incident highlights failures in secrets management, credential monitoring, and access control practices relevant to IAM and privileged access management teams.
